purpose: Perphenazine is used to treat schizophrenia and to help control severe nausea and vomiting. It can help reduce symptoms like hallucinations, confused thinking, and agitation. Doctors may also use it for other conditions as they see fit.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical messenger called dopamine to send signals between nerve cells. In conditions like schizophrenia, there can be too much dopamine activity in certain areas. Perphenazine works by blocking dopamine receptors, which helps calm down those overactive signals and reduce symptoms.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or feeling sleepy, dizziness when standing up, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, and weight gain. Some people may notice muscle stiffness, restlessness, or unusual muscle movements, especially early in treatment. Let your doctor know if any of these bother you.
warnings: This medication can cause serious muscle movement problems called tardive dyskinesia, which may be permanent, so report any unusual movements right away. It can make you more sensitive to heat, so avoid getting overheated. Elderly patients with dementia who take this type of medication have a higher risk of stroke or death. Do not drink alcohol while taking it, and always tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as interactions can occur. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: For schizophrenia, a common starting dose is 4 to 8 mg taken by mouth two to three times a day, adjusted by your doctor based on how you respond. For nausea and vomiting, lower doses are typically used. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose will be tailored to your individual needs.
